notes: The circuit image shows no breadboard; the parts list gives 2 mini breadboards. I used one breadboard (bb1) only to join the two I2C lines and the two 4.7k pull-up resistors, and used jumper wires for every wire in the image.

A4 is SDA and A5 is SCL on both boards. Each line (A4 together, A5 together) is shared by both boards and has one 4.7k resistor to 3V3. In the image the resistors' lower ends are tied to the red 3V wire from the reader's 3V pin.
The two Nano boards are not placed on a breadboard, as the image shows them standalone with wires to their header pins.
Both boards are powered and programmed over USB cables to a computer. The computer is not modelled, so the USB cables only connect to the boards.
The Nano 33 BLE Sense catalogue entry has a single GND port, used for both GND connections. The image's '3V' pin is mapped to port 3V3. Only the Reader's 3V is wired.
Both boards are described as Nano 33 BLE / BLE Sense, so both use the arduino-nano-33-ble-sense type.
The breadboard rail holes tp.1, tp.2 and tp.3 are all on one top-power rail strip, which carries the 3V3 supply.
